advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Route the `fields()` discovery call through `_call_logged`/`_with_connection_retry` so it gets the same retry, error translation, and WARNING logging as every other REST access in the transport.
evidence: transport.py:715-718 calls `lister()` directly inside a generator, with no `_call_logged`/`_with_connection_retry` wrapper: `self._epic_link_field_id = next((f.get("id") for f in lister() if f.get("name") == "Epic Link"), None,)`
Every other REST call in the module IS wrapped, e.g. transport.py:698 `issue = _call_logged("set_parent", remote_id, lambda: self._client.issue(remote_id))` and transport.py:734/737 for the update.

`_call_logged` docstring (transport.py:179-189): runs `fn()` through `_with_connection_retry` and 'This log is the only signal those paths emit' for the parent/comment/link members that core swallows.
Module docstring (transport.py:25-29): a connection-level fault is retried up to 2 times; an HTTP error is translated. A raw `fields()` gets neither retry nor `_as_backend_http_error` translation.
advisory.finding: The Epic Link field-discovery call (`lister()`) bypasses `_call_logged`/`_with_connection_retry`, so unlike every other REST access in this transport it is not connection-retried, its errors are not translated to `BackendHTTPError`, and it emits no member-named WARNING on failure.
scenarios: A transient network blip or TLS reset during `GET /rest/api/2/field` fails the whole `set_parent` where a retry would have recovered it.

A JIRAError from field discovery propagates as an untranslated `jira.JIRAError` (not `BackendHTTPError`) and produces no member-named WARNING, so the failure is less observable than the mutation it precedes.
advisory.suggested_fix: Wrap the discovery in the same choke point, e.g. `entries = _call_logged("set_parent", remote_id, lambda: lister())` then compute `self._epic_link_field_id = next((f.get("id") for f in entries if f.get("name") == "Epic Link"), None)`.

evidence: transport.py:707-718 distinguishes `_MISSING` from `None` so 'a lookup that finds nothing is cached too — see `_MISSING` above' (comment line 710), making negative-caching an explicit load-bearing design point
test_the_epic_link_field_is_discovered_once_not_per_call (line 168-185) asserts `client.field_calls == 1` but only with `_FakeClient(subtask=False)` where Epic Link IS present

test_an_undiscoverable_epic_link_declines_and_never_writes_fields_parent (line 235) constructs `epic_link_name=None` but calls `set_parent` exactly once (line 247), so it never checks that a second call skips re-discovery
ABSENCE: search for `field_calls` shows the only count assertion is at line 182 (positive path); no test drives >1 set_parent against an epic_link-absent client to assert field_calls stays 1
advisory.finding: The negative-cache branch — a fieldless instance caches `None` and is NOT re-probed on subsequent set_parent calls — has no regression coverage; `field_calls` is asserted only when the Epic Link field IS found.
scenarios: A refactor that caches only found field ids (e.g. `if field_id is not None: self._epic_link_field_id = field_id`) would re-probe fields() on every set_parent for a fieldless instance — the exact REST-cost regression ticket b586 motivated — and every existing test would still pass
advisory.suggested_fix: Add test_a_fieldless_instance_is_not_reprobed: build `_FakeClient(subtask=False, epic_link_name=None)`, call `set_parent` three times (catching NotImplementedError each), then assert `client.field_calls == 1`.
